Treatment field marks Collins good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
Lake record verifies Rawlings v. Kentucky, 448 U.S. 98, status verified.
Treatment field marks Rawlings good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
Lake record verifies Samson v. California, 547 U.S. 843, status verified.
Treatment field marks Samson good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
Lake record verifies United States v. Salvucci, 448 U.S. 83, status verified.
Treatment field marks Salvucci good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
Lake record verifies United States v. Payner, 447 U.S. 727, status verified.
Treatment scope says a federal court may not use supervisory power to evade Fourth Amendment standing rules and marks Payner good_law as of 2026-06-30.
Lake record verifies Minnesota v. Olson, 495 U.S. 91, status verified.
Treatment field marks Olson good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
Lake record verifies Alderman v. United States, 394 U.S. 165, status verified.
Treatment scope says the personal-rights standing rule remains good law and that Rakas reaffirmed Alderman's core principle.
Lake record verifies Mancusi v. DeForte, 392 U.S. 364, status verified.
Treatment scope says the shared-workplace reasonable-expectation holding survives and was not disturbed by Rakas.
Lake record verifies Rakas v. Illinois, 439 U.S. 128, status verified.
Treatment field marks Rakas good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
Lake record verifies Simmons v. United States, 390 U.S. 377, status verified.
Treatment scope says the suppression-hearing testimony immunity remains good law.
Lake record verifies Jones v. United States, 362 U.S. 257, status verified.

Lake treatment marks Jones superseded and specifically says automatic standing was overruled by Salvucci and broad legitimately-on-premises standing was disavowed by Rakas, matching the page's history-only label.
Lake record verifies Katz v. United States, 389 U.S. 347, status verified.
Treatment scope says Katz's reasonable-expectation framework remains governing, while noting trespass is an additional basis that does not disturb Katz.
residual_risks: Katz should not be framed as the exclusive search-definition path because the lake scope note recognizes a revived trespass theory.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If space permits, say Katz supplies the REP measure, not the exclusive Fourth Amendment search theory.

reasons: Lake record verifies Minnesota v. Carter, 525 U.S. 83, status verified.
Treatment field marks Carter good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
Lake record verifies United States v. Padilla, 508 U.S. 77, status verified.
Treatment scope says Padilla rejects the coconspirator exception and remains good law.
Lake record verifies Brendlin v. California, 551 U.S. 249, status verified.
Treatment field marks Brendlin good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides.
Lake record verifies Byrd v. United States, 584 U.S. 395, status verified.
Treatment field marks Byrd good_law as of 2026-06-30 with no point overrides; the page's wording already limits the rule to lawful possession and control.
Currency-only review: Rakas is verified and marked good_law as of 2026-06-30.
Katz is verified and marked good_law; Alderman's lake treatment also confirms the personal-rights standing rule remains good law.
residual_risks: Support and quote fidelity were not evaluated under Lens B.
The Katz lake scope note recognizes trespass as an additional search theory, so the rule should avoid implying REP is exclusive beyond the standing context.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Avoid exclusive phrasing around Katz where the page is speaking about all Fourth Amendment search theories rather than REP standing.
